turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
i've been dragging for months... sleep all night and still wake up wrecked.. missed my friend's birthday drinks last week, left the group chat unread, then called out of my opening shift because getting dressed felt impossible.

people need help when they're actually dealing with something. for me it's the lazy unreliable version. if i said it out loud, my friends and manager would see exactly what i am. weak.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: the part about “getting dressed felt impossible” caught me. i had a year where i sat on the floor before work with one sock on, convinced the day was already over; it took time, but now mornings don’t get to make every decision for me.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: one sock on is too close... except i don't get back up. i stared at my uniform on the chair until my shift started and then lied that my stomach was bad.. that's not a rough morning, that's being the person nobody can count on.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: when you stared at the uniform and then called out, what was the first part that locked up: standing, showering, leaving, or facing people after being gone?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: facing people. walking in late means everyone knows i couldn't do a normal morning.. my manager trusts me with opening drawers and i can't even open my eyes on time. that makes me unsafe to trust.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: you narrowed it to the exact point where it spikes: facing people after being gone. that’s a lot more specific than only staring at the alarm.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: specific doesn't change it. i still left my coworker alone for the first rush.. she had to text me “are you coming” while i was under a blanket. shame hits because the thing is true. i'm dead weight.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: getting that “are you coming” text while you’re under a blanket is a brutal little snapshot. you don’t have to turn it into a whole speech to your roommate or friends tonight.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: i won't tell them. my roommate heard me fake the stomach thing on the phone and i said it was nothing.. saying the real reason would make me the broken roommate who can't handle a schedule. it costs more than it fixes.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: when your roommate heard the call and you said “nothing,” what were you protecting most: your job image, the apartment peace, or the version of you they already know?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: the version they already know. they think i'm tired from shifts and school, not the person who skips birthdays and leaves coworkers alone because a blanket wins. if i ask for help, it confirms i'm not built like normal people.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
i did go in yesterday... kept thinking about the “facing people after being gone” thing.

at work it's not just a feeling. i left my coworker alone and everyone saw my manager watching if i could handle closing. if they knew the real reason, it would confirm i'm unreliable.

outside of work idk... in my room it sometimes feels like my body is doing this to me, not me choosing it. but behind the counter i'm the weak link.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: “behind the counter i'm the weak link” is exactly the sentence i used to have about myself on every shift. for a while the schedule ran my whole day, but later i got to where a bad morning didn't get to decide the whole shift for me.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
a bad morning not deciding the whole shift sounds fake from here... but i did make it through 5 hours after standing in the stockroom pretending to check boxes.

then i counted the drawer twice and my coworker watched me do it. at work that proves i'm not safe to rely on.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: when you made it through those 5 hours, was there one part that kept you from leaving: the boxes, staying out of eye contact, or just having a next tiny task?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
the boxes, probably. no one looks at you when you're matching labels.. one carton, then another.

outside the floor maybe it's like my brain stalls, idk. but once i'm on register and slow, customers wait and my coworker fixes it. that's me failing the job.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: you found a low-eye-contact task and used it to stay in the building. that's not nothing, even if the register still felt like it exposed every shaky part.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
using boxes sounds too generous lol... i hid in the stockroom until someone needed change.

my manager asked if i was okay and i said “just tired.” saying the real reason at work would tell her exactly why not to schedule me alone.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: “just tired” may have been the only answer you could get out in that second. her scheduling choices still don't get to be the whole verdict on what kind of person you are.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
i want to believe the “not the whole verdict” part somewhere else... like my roommate just thought i had an early shift when i went quiet and didn't make it a thing.

so at home idk, maybe it isn't written on me. but at work it is. they pay me to be steady and i'm not.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: when your roommate didn't make it a thing, what did you do after that quiet part? i'm curious if anything kept the spiral from taking the whole room.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
i changed out of my work shirt and washed a cup that had been on my desk for days... glamorous recovery arc lol.

it kept me from crawling back under the blanket for like 10 minutes. idk, maybe that part is just a thing happening to me, something i can interrupt once in a while. but work is different. if they find out why i disappear, it confirms i'm the unreliable one.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
i tried the not-crawling-back-under-the-blanket thing after my shift... made tea, opened a text from a friend asking if i wanted to hang out this week, then just stared at it.

outside work idk, sometimes it feels like my body shuts the door before i choose anything. but work is different. if anyone there knew i'm avoiding people after shifts because i can't move, it proves i'm not dependable.

and then i don't answer friends either, so... social trash panda but less cute.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Opening the text and freezing there is a stuck place, not a final ruling on you. You get to choose whether she gets a tiny reply, a later reply, or no reply tonight; none of those has to explain your whole life.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
tiny reply sounds less impossible than the whole life version... i typed “been wiped, sorry” and deleted it like 4 times.

with her idk maybe it just sounds like a bad week. at work saying i'm wiped tells them exactly why i shouldn't be trusted with closing.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: What version would feel least like handing over evidence against yourself: “sorry i vanished,” “can we raincheck,” or something even smaller? I'm asking because the deleted draft already shows you were trying to keep a thread open.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
least awful is probably “sorry i vanished, can we raincheck” because it doesn't say why.

even “low energy” makes me cringe. for a friend idk maybe it's not a confession. at work low energy is me announcing i'm the person who can't handle the job.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: That raincheck sentence protects you from making up a whole fake excuse. Keeping it small can be a way to stay connected without putting yourself on trial.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
i sent it before i could make it a dissertation lol. she hearted it and said “no worries.”

i still feel like i'm being the friend people stop inviting because i'm always half missing. idk maybe today it was just a delayed text and not me being garbage. but work isn't like that. work needs me there and steady, and i'm not.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: I used to answer people days late and assume every heart reaction was pity or the last warning before they gave up. A couple people kept leaving the door cracked for me longer than I believed they would.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
the door cracked thing is weirdly the part i keep looking at... she didn't ask for a reason or do the “where have you been” thing.

i put my phone face down instead of deleting the thread. idk maybe with her i can be a little absent and not instantly cut off. at work being absent is the problem.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Leaving the thread there is enough of a next step for tonight; you don't have to make it into a big honest talk. And the work fear can be loud without getting to name every part of you.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
yeah... leaving it there is probably the most i can do tonight.

i still don't want anyone from work knowing. they depend on me to be steady and i'm not. with my friend idk, maybe answering late doesn't have to be the whole story. i'm still hiding a lot.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
update from the raincheck: she sent "want to do coffee after class? no pressure" and i opened it at lunch and did the statue thing again.

idk with her maybe it's not proof i'm a terrible friend, just... my brain hitting airplane mode. but work was awful today. manager asked if i could cover closing saturday and i said yes while wanting to crawl under the counter.

if they knew i'm ducking friends because i can't get up after shifts, it proves i'm unreliable. so i don't tell anyone and then i disappear more. genius goblin behavior.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: When I finally told a clinic person I was sleeping through alarms and dodging people, I was sure I was basically admitting I couldn't be trusted. What actually happened was boring and specific: a form, some crying in a chair, and one tiny plan for getting through the next week.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
the "boring and specific" part is hard to picture... i looked up the campus counseling page after reading this and immediately closed it because the intake form said "reason for visit" and my reason is basically "can't human."

for school idk maybe people fill those out when they're messy. at work there is no plain version. if my manager hears i sleep through life after shifts, i am the weak link.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: If you opened that form again someday, what would be the smallest true phrase that doesn't turn it into your whole life story? Like, not polished, just enough for the box.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
smallest true phrase would be "tired all the time and avoiding people" maybe... typing that here makes me want to throw my phone in soup.

with a form idk maybe that's what the box is for. with work, "tired all the time" is a confession. they need someone steady and i'm not.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: You found a sentence that's true and not an essay. That split you named matters too: a form and your manager don't have to get the same amount of you.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
i like "same amount" more than "confess everything"... i answered her finally with "coffee might be too much, could do a walk near campus?" and then muted the chat like a brave little coward.

idk maybe with her that's just being specific. at work i don't get to choose amounts. they get my whole performance and it shows i'm dragging.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: A walk instead of coffee is you making the plan smaller, not disappearing from it. You can mute the chat and still have left something open.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
she said walk is good and sent a leaf emoji lol. i didn't delete it.

idk maybe that's a normal person amount of contact? but i'm still not telling my roommate why i've been eating cereal in bed. if work sees this version of me, it confirms i'm not built for the schedule.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: I spent a long time thinking the cereal-in-bed weeks were the real me and the version who answered people was fake. Later it got less either/or; I still had rough nights, but they stopped automatically cancelling every plan.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
cereal-in-bed weeks being the real me is exactly where my head goes... tonight i put the bowl in the sink before my roommate got home, which is pathetic but also better than leaving evidence lol.

idk maybe the walk can exist next to that without me explaining everything. work still feels different. if they knew how much i'm hiding just to look normal, they'd be right not to count on me.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
walk update... i went. we did the tiny loop near campus and i said i've been tired and weird lately, not the full cereal-in-bed museum exhibit.

she didn't make a face. she just said low-key was good and kept walking with me.

so idk... the whole "needing help means weak/lazy" thing has a dent in it maybe? because she saw a slice of it and still treated me normal. but i also opened the counseling form again and the "reason for visit" box made me feel like i was putting a loser sticker on my own forehead. confused goblin.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: When I first wrote to a counselor, I thought the reason box was where I proved I was lazy and not coping. In the appointment it ended up being boringly practical: sleep, missed plans, shifts, and one next step, not a verdict on me.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
"not a verdict" makes the box sound less cursed... i typed "tired all the time, missing plans, getting behind" into my notes app instead of the form.

phone did not explode. annoying.

but hitting submit still feels like admitting i failed basic adulting. like congrats, i need a grown-up receipt.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: You turned the scary box into words you could hold somewhere else first. That's practice with being honest, not a trial where you have to prove you're fine.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
practice is a nicer word than trial... i left it in notes.

i also didn't call out today even though i wanted to. sold socks under fluorescent punishment and only cried in the stockroom for like 40 seconds, classy.

if i'm lazy, why am i dragging myself through shifts? but also a useful person probably doesn't need applause for showing up. idk.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: On days you drag yourself through shifts, what usually gets you from bed to the door? Alarm, roommate noise, needing the paycheck, spite, something else?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
mostly paycheck panic... today it was my roommate making toast and me not wanting them to see me fossilized in bed at 11.

which is dumb because shame as fuel is trash fuel. but it did get me up.

so maybe i'm not broken-broken... just running on the worst battery pack.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Trash fuel can get you through a day, but it doesn't have to be the only fuel you ever get. Shame being loud right now doesn't get to write the final report on you.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
final report... yeah. my friend texted after the walk, "glad we did low-key" and i keep rereading it like evidence lol.

she knows i was off and she didn't downgrade me. so maybe the weak/lazy label is not the whole file.

still can't picture saying any of this to my roommate. that feels like opening a trapdoor.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: I used to reread one calm reply from a friend like it was a tiny receipt that I wasn't automatically getting kicked out for being messy. It didn't make home conversations easy, but it made the next small truth feel less impossible.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
next small truth maybe is not roommate yet... too big.

but i put the notes-app sentence in the counseling draft and saved it, no submit yet. weirdly, the walk text and the fact i worked today are both annoying little counterarguments to "i'm just lazy."

i still feel fake asking for anything. but it isn't closing as cleanly as it used to. exhausted raccoon.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
form update... i opened the counseling draft again after work and did not immediately fling my phone into the sea.

still no submit. but i added the notes-app sentence into the actual box: tired all the time, missing plans, getting behind.

i keep rereading my friend's "glad we did low-key" text like a tiny court document. she saw me being weird and didn't downgrade me. if i was just lazy maybe i wouldn't be doing this weird paperwork obstacle course?

but the submit button still feels like a loser stamp. paperwork gremlin.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: You opened the draft after work, put the plain facts in the scary box, and left them there. That is effort happening in the exact place where shame wants you to disappear.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
"plain facts" helps a little... the box looks boring when it's typed out. no dropdown for tragic idiot, rude.

i added "trouble getting out of bed" too and then stared at it like it was evidence against me.

but also... evidence of me not pretending? idk. my thumb still hovers like the button has teeth.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: When your thumb hovers there, what keeps you from deleting the whole thing? Is it the friend text, the wording feeling more boring, or something else?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
mostly the friend text... and maybe spite at this point.

i usually delete stuff the second i feel exposed. like whole drafts, whole tabs, dramatic little digital bonfire.

this one is still there. that feels tiny but not nothing. still pathetic that a form needs a support audience, but yeah.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: A support audience for the scariest click doesn't make you pathetic. It means you found a way to keep one thread from snapping while you decide what to do next.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
"keep one thread" is annoyingly accurate.

i did the tiniest possible next thing: changed the sentence so it sounds like a human wrote it, saved again, left the laptop open.

not submitted. not brave movie montage. but i didn't slam it shut like it was radioactive.

maybe the label in my head is louder than the actual evidence. actual evidence is me trying, annoyingly.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: I had a stretch where the ugly label in my head sounded more official than anything I actually did. The boring receipts were what started making it less convincing; yours today are saved sentence, open laptop, still here.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
boring receipts lol.

i wrote them in notes because apparently i'm making a case file now: worked shift, answered my friend's low-key text, saved the form sentence, did laundry halfway. washed it and then abandoned the wet dragon, very professional.

none of that screams thriving. but it also doesn't scream lazy corpse. i hate that i can see both.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: When you can see both, which receipt feels least fake to you: the shift, the saved sentence, the friend text, or even the wet-dragon laundry?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
least fake is the saved sentence.

because nobody saw it, so it wasn't me performing functional for work or my friend or whatever. i did it alone and still didn't erase it.

i still don't feel like someone who deserves the appointment exactly... but the lazy/weak thing has to argue with that now.

tired possum with documentation.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
update: i submitted the form.

no confetti, just an auto email with a request number, very glamorous. i almost closed the laptop instead, but the saved sentence from last time was sitting there looking all boring and factual.

part of me says needing an appointment means i'm weak/lazy, but also... i did a shift and then clicked the thing alone. if i was just avoiding life, idk why i would do the gross responsible button.

still feel like a fraud with a ticket number. damp possum escalated.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: How did you get from hover to click when nobody was watching? I’m asking because that exact gap between “saved” and “sent” is the part I never had a clean trick for.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
not clean lol.

i put my phone across the room so i couldn't text anyone dramatically, reread the boring receipts note, and said out loud "just send the boring version" and clicked before the shame paragraph could load.

then i immediately made tea like a victorian ghost. coping, apparently.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: You made it boring on purpose and gave the shame paragraph less time to monologue. That’s a strategy, not a personality defect.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
strategy is generous... but yeah, i did make it boring on purpose.

auto reply says someone will respond in 2-3 business days. my first thought was cancel before a human sees it. second thought was... a human seeing it is the point? rude development.

i don't fully buy that i'm someone who should take a slot. but i didn't withdraw it.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: The “should I take a slot” argument can stay unresolved tonight. You don’t have to win that whole courtroom before you let the request keep existing.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
letting it exist is apparently the activity.

i made a folder called boring receipts and put the confirmation email there because i'm insufferable. the shame voice says this is me making a big production out of being tired.

but the confirmation email is also... me not hiding from it for once. annoying mixed evidence.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: I used to turn every small step into proof I was being dramatic. The record of steps helped later because it showed I wasn’t inventing the bad days or the effort.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
the dramatic thing hits.

i keep thinking the counseling person will read "tired all the time" and be like please try coffee. but then i looked at my notes and it's not one sleepy morning... it's months of missed plans and bed glue and weird form archaeology.

dramatic doesn't explain all of that. still scared they'll think i'm wasting time.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: When you looked at the notes and saw months instead of one sleepy morning, what helped you not shrink it back down right away? I genuinely want to know how you kept it from disappearing again.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
i think the dates helped... calendar receipts are rude.

i wrote down three missed hangouts, two late assignments, and the week i wore the same work shirt twice because laundry was a swamp. that is embarrassing, but it's also too specific to be just "i'm lazy lol".

i still want to disappear before the email comes, but the lazy/weak thing has less room to sit alone now. possum with exhibits.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
email came. actual human offered tuesday at 10 and i stared at it like a court summons.

i opened the boring receipts folder like a little goblin and saw the dates again. part of me still says taking the appointment means i'm weak/lazy and making a production out of being tired.

but the same folder says i missed 3 hangouts and wore the work shirt twice and still submitted the form after a shift. that doesn't fit neatly with "just lazy"... idk.

i haven't replied yet. possum holding a calendar invite.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: What would make the reply boring enough to send, the same way the form became boring enough to click? I’m asking because you’ve been weirdly good at shrinking the scary part down to one plain sentence.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
okay i tried the one plain sentence thing.

i wrote "tuesday at 10 works, thank you" and did not add the paragraph where i explain i'm probably wasting everyone's time. hit send before i could get fancy and pathetic.

then i put the laptop under a hoodie like that helps. very adult.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: You turned it into scheduling, not a confession. And you sent it before the apology essay could take the wheel.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
i hate that scheduling worked lol.

there's now a normal sent email sitting there. no lightning strike, no "actually never mind you are too dramatic" auto-response.

still feels like when they see me they'll know i'm the kind of person who can't handle basic life. but the email itself is annoyingly normal evidence.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: I had a stretch where every normal message felt like it would expose that I was secretly failing at being a person. Over time, the normal messages piled up and made that fear less able to narrate everything.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
"narrate everything" is too accurate.

i went to work after sending it and kept checking my phone in the stockroom like the appointment police were coming. then a friend texted "alive?" and i almost did the usual meme dodge.

instead i said "rough week, appointment thing pending" which felt illegal and also not a whole confession. she just sent a heart and asked if i wanted fries after class.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: How did you land on “appointment thing pending” instead of the meme dodge? That phrase is useful—honest, but not handing someone your whole file.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
i think i stole it from the boring receipts vibe.

"appointment thing pending" sounded like a calendar problem instead of me announcing i'm defective. i typed and deleted it like five times though.

but she didn't treat me like damaged goods... she asked about fries. hard to make that fit with "everyone will think less of me." still trying, because my brain is committed to the bit.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: The fries reply doesn’t erase the fear, but it does give the fear competition. You found a size of truth you could actually send to one person.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text:
yeah... competition is the word.

i'm not magically proud of this. i still feel gross about the intake and i might try to cancel in my head 80 times before tuesday.

but the evidence pile is annoying now: request number, normal email, friend offering fries, me showing up to shift anyway. weak/lazy is still loud, just not the only exhibit.

damp possum, but with a folder.
